name: Replace Activity (registry-quality)
description: Sibling #6 of the registry-quality-pass per OpenSpec change 2026-04-27-activity-registry-quality-pass. Consumes activityReview[] (severity 2-3 — idiom-aligned but improvable) plus pattern[] (from extract-pattern) and synthesizes activityTemplateProposal entries. Five tasks: (1) acquire_targets_and_patterns — impulse-resolve both shapes from the pool; (2) match_patterns_to_reviews — llm; for each review, picks the best pattern as a replacement template's basis; emits matchedReview[] (review + matched pattern); (3) synthesize_replacements — iteration; body=llm generates new template JSON proposals (NOT a write — emits activityTemplateProposal shape; never directly writes; the user/operator decides); aggregateAs=list; (4) validate_proposals — iteration; body=llm validates each proposal against compliance rules; tags valid: true|false; (5) emit_proposals — emits activityTemplateProposal[] + auditReport + goalEnd. CONTEXT-BUDGET: each per-review LLM body is bounded at maxTokens=900 (template proposals are larger than reviews/concepts but still bounded); per-validation pass at maxTokens=400. PROPOSAL-NOT-WRITE posture: this activity NEVER calls activityTemplate_write — it surfaces proposals for an operator (or a downstream activity invoking make-activity) to decide.

variables.name: maxProposals
variables.description: Maximum number of activityTemplateProposal entries to synthesize per invocation. The match_patterns_to_reviews task selects the top-N reviews (sorted by improvement potential — typically severity 2-3 with the strongest matched pattern) and synthesize_replacements iterates over those N. Default 5 keeps a single invocation's iteration body within ~5 LLM calls (each capped at maxTokens=900), totalling ~4.5K output tokens. Lower (e.g. 3) for a fast smoke; higher (e.g. 10) for a comprehensive sweep at higher cost.

variables.name: requireValidation
variables.description: When true (the default), validate_proposals runs and tags each proposal with valid: true|false. When false, validate_proposals is skipped via conditional and emit_proposals surfaces all synthesized proposals untagged. Recommended: keep true so that downstream consumers (workbench, make-activity dispatch) see the validation verdict alongside the proposal.

pointer.content: Acquire activityReview[] (from scored_reviews) AND pattern[] (from patterns_list) via impulse pool reference.

tasks.notes: Read the activityReview[] (severity 2-3 idiom-aligned candidates from review-activity's score_severity task — referenced in the pool as scored_reviews) AND pattern[] (from extract-pattern's extract_patterns task — referenced as patterns_list) from the impulse pool. Same pool-by-id pattern as the rest of this activity family. The pointer's type=`memo` is a placeholder; downstream LLM calls reference {{impulse:scored_reviews}} and {{impulse:patterns_list}} directly. When either shape is empty (review-activity OR extract-pattern not run in current session), the chain still completes with a goalEnd describing the no-op (zero proposals).

tasks.description: LLM task that pairs each severity 2-3 review with the best-fit pattern from patterns_list.

config.prompt:
You are pairing severity 2-3 activity reviews with reusable patterns to identify replacement candidates.

VARIABLES:
- maxProposals = {{maxProposals}}

REVIEWS (filter to severity in [2, 3]):
{{impulse:scored_reviews}}

PATTERNS:
{{impulse:patterns_list}}

FOR EACH severity 2-3 review, pick the best matching pattern.

MATCH HEURISTIC:
- review.summary describes a deficiency (e.g. 'all-LLM task chain', 'missing inputShapes')
- pattern.applicability describes when the pattern fits
- Score (0..1) on applicability fit; drop matches < 0.5 as 'no good replacement found'

Return the top-{{maxProposals}} matches by match_score.

Output EXACTLY this JSON (no markdown, no prose):
{"matchedReviews":[{"review":<review object>,"matched_pattern":<pattern object>,"match_score":<0..1>,"rationale":"<one-sentence explanation citing review.findings + pattern.applicability>"}],"unmatched":[<review objects with no match >= 0.5>]}

tasks.notes: Match heuristic: review.summary describes a deficiency (e.g. 'all-LLM task chain where deterministic resolver would suffice', 'missing inputShapes declaration'); pattern.applicability describes when the pattern fits (e.g. 'when goal requires iterating over a list of impulses'); the LLM scores each (review, pattern) pair on applicability fit and emits the best pair per review. Drops reviews with no good match (score < 0.5 in the LLM's judgment) — these are flagged for prune-activity instead. Output: matchedReviews list of {review, matched_pattern, match_score, rationale}, capped at maxProposals (top-N by match_score). SIMPLIFICATION: a deterministic `pattern_review_matcher` resolver consuming the structured fields of both impulses is the proper fix; today the LLM applies the heuristic and is bounded at maxTokens=1500 over the full input set.

config.prompt:
You are synthesizing an activityTemplate proposal that REPLACES an existing template by addressing its review deficiencies using a matched pattern as a blueprint.

MATCH (review + matched_pattern):
{{match}}

OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS:
- Emit a structurally valid activityTemplate JSON object (NOT a write — this is a proposal for review)
- id — original templateId + '-v2' OR a derived unique id
- name — derived from original; reflect the pattern (e.g. 'Foo (iterate-aggregate)')
- description — 2-4 sentences citing what was wrong with the original AND how the pattern fixes it
- category — copy from original (in match.review)
- version — '0.1.0' (this is a NEW template, not a variant)
- tags — copy original tags + add 'registry-quality-replacement'
- variables — derive from original + the pattern's task_graph_shape requirements
- tasks — synthesize from pattern.task_graph_shape; each task must declare resolver, inputShapes, outputShapes; bash/file resolvers reference {{variables.workingDirectory}} for path arguments (sandbox hygiene)
- metadata — set author='replace-activity', source_review_id=<review.templateId>, source_pattern_id=<pattern.name>, openSpec='2026-04-27-activity-registry-quality-pass'

CRITICAL: declare every task's inputShapes and outputShapes; no naked LLM tasks; no hard-coded paths outside workingDirectory; no all-LLM task chains where a deterministic resolver fits.

Output EXACTLY this JSON (no markdown, no prose):
{"id":"<...>","name":"<...>","description":"<...>","category":"<...>","version":"0.1.0","tags":[...],"variables":[...],"tasks":[...],"metadata":{"author":"replace-activity","source_review_id":"<...>","source_pattern_id":"<...>","openSpec":"2026-04-27-activity-registry-quality-pass"},"_proposal_note":"replacement candidate — NOT yet written; awaits operator review or downstream make-activity dispatch"}

tasks.notes: Iterate over matched_reviews from match_patterns_to_reviews; per-match the LLM body generates a new activityTemplate-shaped JSON proposal that addresses the review's deficiencies using the matched_pattern's structure as a blueprint. The proposal's id is the original review's templateId + '-v2' (or similar — the LLM is instructed to derive a unique id); fields include name, description, category, version, tags, variables, tasks, metadata. CRUCIALLY: this task NEVER calls activityTemplate_write — it emits activityTemplateProposal impulses for downstream consumption (operator review, workbench display, OR a downstream activity that invokes make-activity with the proposal as a goal). aggregateAs=list collects per-match proposals into a single proposals_list impulse. SIMPLIFICATION: a deterministic `template_synthesizer` resolver (mentioned in make-activity.json:openQuestions[1] as a future fix) would replace this LLM body once the synthesis pattern stabilizes; today the LLM is bounded at maxTokens=900 per iteration. The body is instructed to emit STRUCTURALLY VALID activityTemplate JSON; validate_proposals downstream double-checks compliance.

config.prompt:
You are validating an activityTemplate proposal against the registry-quality compliance ruleset.

PROPOSAL:
{{proposal}}

RULES (default ruleset, same as review-activity):
1. idiom_alignment — declares inputShapes/outputShapes; uses resolvers idiomatically (no hand-rolled bash for orchestration); no hard-coded absolute paths outside workingDirectory.
2. shape_completeness — every task declares its inputShapes / outputShapes; no naked LLM tasks emitting unnamed impulses.
3. resolver_diversity — no all-LLM task chains when a deterministic resolver (bash, file, git, impulse-resolve, validation) would suffice.
4. redundancy — does this proposal's output_shapes overlap with another existing template's output_shapes? (Heuristic — if the original template's id+'-v2' suggests a direct replacement, redundancy is acceptable; otherwise flag).
5. sandbox_hygiene — bash/file resolver path arguments reference {{variables.workingDirectory}}.

For each rule, verdict: pass | warn | fail.

overall valid: true if all rules pass or warn; false if ANY rule fails.

Output EXACTLY this JSON (no markdown, no prose):
{"proposal":<proposal object>,"valid":<true|false>,"validation_findings":[{"rule":"<name>","verdict":"pass|warn|fail","detail":"<one-line>"}],"compliance_summary":"<one-sentence overall compliance summary>"}

tasks.notes: Iterate over the proposals from synthesize_replacements; per-proposal the LLM body validates against compliance rules (same default ruleset as review-activity: idiom_alignment, shape_completeness, resolver_diversity, redundancy, sandbox_hygiene). Emits a tag {valid: true|false, validation_findings: [...], compliance_summary: <...>} appended to each proposal. Conditional gate: requireValidation=true (the default). When requireValidation=false, this task is skipped and proposals flow through untagged. SIMPLIFICATION: a deterministic `template_compliance_validator` resolver consuming the proposal JSON would replace this LLM body once the rule set stabilizes (see review-activity openQuestions for the same theme); today the LLM is bounded at maxTokens=400 per iteration. Per-iteration errors do not short-circuit — invalid proposals still flow through to emit_proposals, just tagged valid=false.

tasks.description: LLM summarizes the proposals and emits the final auditReport + goalEnd matching make-activity's emission contract.

config.prompt:
You are emitting the final replacement-proposal report for a replace-activity invocation.

INPUTS:
- MATCHED REVIEWS: {{impulse:matched_reviews}}
- PROPOSALS (synthesize_replacements output): {{impulse:proposals_list}}
- VALIDATED PROPOSALS (validate_proposals output; null when requireValidation=false): {{impulse:validated_proposals}}
- REQUIRE VALIDATION: {{variables.requireValidation}}

Produce a structured audit report with these sections:
1. total_reviews_input — count of severity 2-3 reviews seen
2. total_matched — count of (review, pattern) matches with score >= 0.5
3. total_synthesized — count of proposals generated
4. total_validated — count from validate_proposals (== total_synthesized when requireValidation=false)
5. valid_count — proposals where valid=true (== total_synthesized when requireValidation=false; all flow through untagged-as-valid)
6. invalid_count — proposals where valid=false
7. proposals — array of activityTemplateProposal entries (each with valid tag when requireValidation=true)
8. unmatched — array of severity 2-3 reviews with no good pattern match (forward to prune-activity)
9. forward_pointers — operator/workbench review of proposals; OR make-activity invocation with the proposal as a goal; OR prune-activity for the unmatched

Then call markGoalComplete with:
- summary: 2-3 sentence description (e.g. 'synthesized N proposals from M matched reviews; K passed validation, L failed; J reviews unmatched and forwarded to prune-activity')
- achievedShapes: ['activityTemplateProposal', 'auditReport']
- evidence: array of {kind: 'impulse', ref: <impulse-id>, observation}

Output EXACTLY this JSON (no markdown, no prose):
{"text":"<summary>","achievedShapes":["activityTemplateProposal","auditReport"],"evidence":[<rows>],"goalSucceeded":<true|false>,"completedAt":"<ISO-8601>","auditReport":{"total_reviews_input":<n>,"total_matched":<n>,"total_synthesized":<n>,"total_validated":<n>,"valid_count":<n>,"invalid_count":<n>,"proposals":[...],"unmatched":[...],"forward_pointers":[...]}}

No other fields. No commentary.
config._tool_note: Same prompt-enforced markGoalComplete contract as the rest of this activity family.

tasks.notes: The auditReport carries: total_reviews_input (count of severity 2-3 reviews from acquire_targets_and_patterns), total_matched (count of matched_reviews from match_patterns_to_reviews), total_synthesized (count of proposals from synthesize_replacements), total_validated (count from validate_proposals; equals total_synthesized when requireValidation=false), valid_count, invalid_count, proposals (full list of activityTemplateProposal entries — each with valid tag when requireValidation=true), unmatched (severity 2-3 reviews with no good pattern match — flagged for prune-activity), forward_pointers (operator OR make-activity invocation with proposal as goal; prune-activity for the unmatched). NOTE: this task NEVER calls activityTemplate_write — proposals are surfaced for downstream decision.

metadata.author: activity-registry-quality-pass

newOrInformal: matchedReview — pairing of (review, matched_pattern, match_score, rationale); intermediate shape used by synthesize_replacements

activityTemplateProposal — synthesized template JSON, NOT yet written. The activity surfaces these for operator review or downstream make-activity dispatch. Distinct from activityTemplate (which is a registered shape representing a written template).

openQuestions: PROPOSAL-NOT-WRITE POSTURE: this activity NEVER calls activityTemplate_write — it surfaces proposals for an operator (or a downstream activity) to decide. RATIONALE: synthesizing a replacement template is high-stakes (introduces a new id into the registry); the LLM-generated JSON should be reviewed before persisting. FOLLOW-UP: a sibling activity (apply-replacement, not yet authored) could iterate over validated proposals and dispatch activityTemplate_write per proposal — gated on operator approval OR a Thompson-Sampling-confidence threshold. Alternative: a downstream make-activity dispatch consumes the proposal as a goal and produces a real activityTemplate via its extract_template task.

VALIDATION COVERAGE: validate_proposals applies the same compliance ruleset as review-activity. The redundancy rule is heuristic — when a proposal's id is original-id + '-v2', it's expected to overlap with the original (that's the point of replacement); the LLM is instructed to treat that case as acceptable. FOLLOW-UP: a deterministic `template_compliance_validator` resolver that handles the v2-overlap case explicitly would tighten this.

TEMPLATE SYNTHESIS PROMPT: synthesize_replacements asks the LLM to emit a structurally valid activityTemplate JSON. The structural validity is checked downstream by validate_proposals (and ultimately by the embedded-templates harness if/when the proposal is written). SIMPLIFICATION: the LLM is bounded at maxTokens=900 per iteration which limits how complex the synthesized template can be. FOLLOW-UP: a `template_synthesizer` resolver (also referenced in make-activity.json:openQuestions[1]) consuming the matched_pattern's task_graph_shape and review.findings would replace the LLM body with deterministic synthesis.
MATCH-SCORE THRESHOLD: match_patterns_to_reviews drops matches with score < 0.5. This threshold is hardcoded; FOLLOW-UP: thread as a variable (default 0.5) so operators can tune sensitivity.

UNMATCHED REVIEWS DOWNSTREAM ROUTE: the emit_proposals report flags severity 2-3 reviews with no good pattern match as 'forwarded to prune-activity'. RATIONALE: if a review can't be replaced, it's a candidate for deprecation. SIMPLIFICATION: this activity does not directly invoke prune-activity — operators read the auditReport and decide. FOLLOW-UP: a registry-quality orchestrator could read the unmatched list and dispatch prune-activity with minSeverity=2 (more aggressive).
limitations: PROPOSAL-ONLY — emits activityTemplateProposal impulses + auditReport but does NOT write to the registry. The user/operator (or a downstream make-activity dispatch) decides whether to persist the proposal as a real activityTemplate.
Template synthesis is LLM-derived for first ship; expect minor structural defects until a deterministic template_synthesizer resolver matures. The validate_proposals task surfaces defects.
Match scoring is heuristic — relies on extract-pattern's pattern.applicability descriptions (which are themselves LLM-derived). Treat the matched pairs as informative-not-canonical.
When activityReview[] is empty (review-activity not run) OR pattern[] is empty (extract-pattern not run), the chain emits a goalEnd describing the no-op (zero proposals).
Unmatched severity 2-3 reviews are flagged in the auditReport for prune-activity routing; this activity does not invoke prune-activity directly.
metadata.outputContract: Always emits per-iteration `activityTemplateProposal` impulses (aggregated in proposals_list and validated_proposals) plus an `auditReport` and `goalEnd` for explicit completion. When requireValidation=false, validate_proposals is skipped and the proposals flow through untagged.
metadata.subscriberContract: Not a lifecycle subscriber. Dispatched explicitly — typically after review-activity AND extract-pattern have both completed in the current session, OR in an orchestrated registry-quality sweep.
metadata.spec_reference: OpenSpec change 2026-04-27-activity-registry-quality-pass (sibling #6 of 6). Sibling spec to 2026-04-27-meta-activity-builder.
